nodes.title: Small fixes on docs consistency check
nodes.body:
## Description
The weekly docs check showed a one-line fix as old/new bullets and a multi-line fix as a diff block. Every applied or suggested fix is now a fenced diff block (easier to read). 

Inline math in the posted findings could also break on GitHub in some cases. The description and the doc quote now use GitHub's `` $`...`$ `` form, which Markdown leaves alone. `H$_2$O` becomes `` $`\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}`$ ``. Code spans and `$$...$$` blocks are left as they were. 

## Validation of changes
`pytest tests/test_docs_consistency_triage.py`: all passed. 
`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on the changed files: passed. `python tools/check_test_quality.py --check`: OK.

nodes.title: Apply docs consistency fixes
nodes.body:
## Description
Brings `docs/Explanations/model.md` in line with the source code using the findings of the weekly docs check in #99 after checking each one against the source. Replaces #99.

Corrected:

- The dry adiabat exponent is computed once from the surface composition at $T_s$ and held constant with height (`dry_adiabat_setup.py`).
- $\eta_s$ covers every species. Only condensing species below their critical temperature add the latent-heat and condensate terms of Eq. 5; all others add only $\eta_s c_{p,s}$ (`GeneralAdiabat.py`, `dlnT_dlnP_d`).
- With the water lookup table, $\beta$ for $\mathrm{H_2O}$ is the tabulated $`d\ln p_{\rm sat}/d\ln T`$ (`get_beta`).
- $T_r = 0$ K disables the stratosphere because the tropopause step is skipped for $T_r \le$ `minT`, not because no level reaches 0 K (`compute_moist_adiabat.py`).
- `cpv` defaults to `cp_mode = "constant"`; the Shomate fit applies only with `"T-dependent"` (`cp_funcs.py`).
- The heating rate criterion uses the 50, 30 and 10 K/day thresholds and the top 2% cut-off, not a plain sign change (`find_tropopause.py`).
- The default tropopause temperature is 290 K, not 0 K (`atmosphere_column.py`).

Not fixed: the condensate term of Eq. 5. In `dlnT_dlnP_d` the code multiplies it by an extra $\eta_s$, while the heat capacity sums in `GeneralAdiabat.py` and `set_stratosphere.py` use `x_cond * cp_cond * alpha_cloud` without it, as the doc does. This might be a code issue.

Documentation only; no code changes. 

## Validation of changes
Each changed statement was compared with the code lines named above. I built the documentation site locally to check the rendering.

nodes.title: Adaptations to docs consistency check
nodes.body:
## Description
The weekly docs consistency check turned out to be a little too conservative: many fixes were either filed under 'minor, but needs a manual fix' or under 'serious', which needs a manual fix by default. This meant that hardly any PR was opened, and so the workload of keeping up the docs isn't really reduced. These updates should fix this. It also improves PR/issue readability and reduces spam.

- The prompt now asks for a fix on every minor inconsistency (nothing that isn't backed by the doc or code), and a doc-side suggestion for serious ones. Serious suggestions are listed in the PR but never applied, since the code itself might be wrong.
- If a docs-consistency PR is already open, new fixes are added to it one by one instead of being dropped. A fix the PR already has is not added again.
- Scheduled runs are skipped when the doc, the reviewed source files and the check itself haven't changed since the last scheduled run.
- PR and issue updates are added to the description instead of posted as new comments, so there are no weekly notifications. New serious findings still get a short comment.
- Readability fixes: equations in descriptions are Latex; a doc quote cut from inside an equation is always shown as the whole equation instead of parts, and no em or en dashes (they are ugly imo).
- Triage now refuses fixes that split a wrapped sentence at a line break. It also accepts code quotes that join separate blocks with a `...` line and it now shows multi-line fixes as diff blocks.

## Validation of changes
`tests/test_docs_consistency_triage.py` passes (59 tests). I also checked that the tests fail when the new logic is broken on purpose, and simulated the open-PR update including a fix a reviewer had corrected.

I also ran the analysis and triage locally three times against the current docs (without posting anything).
The workflow changes only run on GitHub, so the first scheduled run after merging is the real test.

## Checklist

- [x] I have followed the [contributing guidelines](https://proteus-framework.org/PROTEUS/CONTRIBUTING.html#how-do-i-contribute)
- [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings or errors
- [x] I have checked that the tests still pass on my computer
- [ ] I have updated the docs, as appropriate
- [x] I have added tests for these changes, as appropriate
- [x] I have checked that all dependencies have been updated, as required

## Relevant people

@nichollsh @egpbos @maraattia I added you all as reviewers since Tim is on leave, if one of you could take a look for me that would be great :) thanks in advance!

nodes.title: Cite papers in the JANUS docs with one footnote form
nodes.body:
## Summary

The JANUS docs cited papers with numbered footnotes and no author or year, with inline journal fields, and with author-year mentions that had no footnote. The 3 affected pages now use one form: the author and year in the text, followed by a footnote with the authors, the linked title, journal, volume, pages, year and the SciX link. No statement or equation in the prose changes; the one number that changes is a section pointer inside `model.md` (below).

## Changes

- `docs/Explanations/model.md`, `docs/Validation/solve_pt.md`, `docs/Tutorials/first_run.md`: 13 papers and 2 books cited as footnotes; the bare markers get the author and year in front of them, and equation pointers sit inside the citation, as in "(Nicholls et al. 2024, Eq. 8)".
- The DOI of Nakajima et al. (1992) was cut after `(1992)049` and did not resolve; it is now the full DOI.
- In `model.md`, a pointer to "Section 3.2" for the moist pseudoadiabat now points to the page's own Section 3.3, and the image alt text no longer carries a footnote marker (it left a back-link with no target).
- The mention of Allen's Astrophysical Quantities (2002) names a book title, not an author, so its line (`model.md:196`) carries `<!-- docs-check: ignore -->`.
- `docs/stylesheets/footnotes.css`: the footnote back-link takes no line space, only the first back-link of each footnote shows, and each footnote has 1 em of right padding, as in FormingWorlds/MORS#69.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `docs-check $(git ls-files 'docs/*.md')` | 14 reference faults on `main` daf22e7c, 0 on the tip, 20 pages |
| Crossref (`api.crossref.org/works/<DOI>`) | full title of all 15 DOIs agree; surnames, volume, pages and year agree where the record holds them |
| ADS search by bibcode (`api.adsabs.harvard.edu/v1/search/bigquery`) | all 14 SciX bibcodes found; titles, surnames, volumes and years agree (Allen's Astrophysical Quantities has no SciX link) |
| Each old numbered marker against the new key at the same place, by DOI or by author and year | the same paper everywhere, except the removed alt-text marker, the completed Nakajima DOI and the new markers where `main` had none |
| Word-level diff of the 3 pages, markers and definitions removed | only author names, years, "et al.", parentheses, the moved equation pointers, the Section 3.3 pointer, the ignore comment and the removed inline journal fields of `solve_pt.md` change; the set of cited equation numbers is the same |
| `zensical build` (0.0.39) | 6 warnings on the tip, 7 on `main` |
| Footnotes in a browser (Playwright, `document.elementFromPoint` at each back-link), 5 pages, 121 widths from 320 to 1520 px | 2420 of 2420 first back-links clicked at their own position, 0 back-links on an empty line, 0 later back-links shown, 0 back-links without a target, 0 widths with a horizontal scroll |

## Size

Added lines, from `pr-breakdown daf22e7c bd19c702`:

| Category | Files | Lines added / removed | Size on disk (KiB) | Compressed (KiB) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| docs text | 4 | +66 / -47 | +4.6 | +1.6 |
